newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Oct-Mar crude throughput seen slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Japan Oct-Mar crude throughput seen slightly lower.

text.p: Top Japanese refiners plan to process slightly less crude during the six months to March compared to the same period a year earlier, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Tuesday.
They plan to process about 0.01 percent less crude during the six-month period, according to a survey of 14 refiners by the ministry.
The refiners processed 128 million kilolitres, or 4.4 million barrels per day, of crude from October 1995 to March 1996, according to the Petroleum Association of Japan.
Oil industry sources said the refiners, who are suffering from huge falls in profits, are keeping crude runs low, partly to keep oil product stockpiles tight and cut costs.
Tight supplies would also help push up domestic retail prices, they said.
Refiners' profits have shrunk because rising global crude prices are pushing costs up while domestic oil product retail prices remain weak.
In October, MITI forecast Japan's demand for oil products during the October-March period would fall 1.3 percent from the same period in the previous year to 132 million kl.
